absent: Exact timing and scheduling of reclaim workers, monitors and page cache fill beyond initialization and scan accounting.
Complete slow path allocation, slab creation, partial list management and page allocator interaction.
Detailed sheaf refill, barn insertion, spare lifecycle and oversize handling beyond extraction and flush.
Debug enforcement for consistency checks, red zones, poison patterns and user tracking storage.
Memory control and tagging hook internals plus object extension reference handling.
Sysfs, debugfs, tracepoint and probe integration behavior beyond stub and call site presence.
NUMA placement, node mismatch handling and strict NUMA enforcement specifics.

findings.text: Provides a cache allocation entry that associates the new object with a list based reclaim domain. It builds a small allocation context carrying caller identity, original size, default disposition and the supplied reclaim pointer, then delegates to the node allocator with no node preference and emits an allocation trace.

Provides a cache allocation entry pinned to an explicit node. It builds the same allocation context shape with default disposition and original size derived from the cache, delegates to the node allocator for the requested node and emits an allocation trace.

Provides a charging wrapper that ensures an already allocated object is accounted to memory control groups. It reports success immediately when the memory control charging path is offline, otherwise it forwards the object and allocation flags to the slab post charge helper and returns that outcome.

Provides bulk allocation from per CPU sheaf storage. It attempts to take up to the requested count from the current CPU main sheaf, records fastpath statistics per batch, and returns how many were satisfied. When the main sheaf is empty it may swap in a usable spare or exchange with the node barn. If neither yields objects it returns the partial count so the caller can continue from slab pages.

Boot time initializer for deferred reclaim of slab and virtual mappings. It creates an unbound reclaim workqueue, clamps a page cache fill delay into a zero to one hundred second window with an informational message when adjusted, initializes per CPU batch arrays and list heads plus monitor and page cache workers, marks each CPU state ready, then allocates and registers a shrinker for this reclaim path.

Shrinker scan callback for deferred reclaim state. It walks possible CPUs, sums pending object counts and drained page cache entries per CPU, triggers the per CPU monitor synchronously, subtracts the per CPU total from the scan budget and accumulates freed totals, stopping early once the budget is exhausted.

Kernel command line handler for slab debugging options plus its parameter operations descriptor. It parses flag lists with optional slab name filters, distinguishes global versus per slab requests, preserves compatibility when only per slab lists appear, updates global debug state and stored filter string, toggles a static branch for debug enablement, requests early stack storage when user tracking is needed and notes poison precedence over auto init.

CPU hotplug handlers for sheaf barn management. Setup checks a node mask quickly then under mutex creates missing per node barn structures for sheaf capable caches, initializes each barn and records the node, with failure reported as out of memory. Dead state walks caches under mutex and flushes the departed CPU main, spare and deferred reclaim sheaves.
Allocation context passed toward the node allocator. It carries caller return address, original request size, allocation disposition flags and an optional reclaim list pointer.
Bulk context for harvesting from partial slabs. It carries allocation flags, minimum and maximum object bounds and an embedded list used to collect candidate slabs.
Iterator over objects within a slab for debug or traversal. It carries a position index and a start pointer, plus optional random freelist traversal state when that configuration is active.

Allocation tracking record and its operation tag. The record carries caller address, optional stack depot handle, CPU and process identity and a timestamp. The tag distinguishes allocation from free. A small constant defines how many addresses are retained per location.

Statistics vocabulary and per cache counters. One enumeration names fast versus slow allocation and free outcomes, slab acquisition and release, node mismatch, fallback and exchange failure, plus detailed sheaf and barn transit events terminated by a count sentinel. A companion structure holds one counter per event, and a separate two valued enumeration selects head versus tail insertion.
Per node store of reusable sheaves. It holds a spin lock, separate lists for full and empty sheaves and counts for each list.

Dynamically sized container of object pointers exchanged between CPUs and nodes. It overlays a reclaim head, a barn list link, a lockless list node and a prefill descriptor carrying capacity and a pfmemalloc marker, then records owning cache, current size, home node for deferred reclaim use and a trailing flexible array of object pointers.

Per CPU sheaf working set. It holds a local lock, a main sheaf that is always present while unlocked, an optional spare that is either empty or full and an optional batch used to defer frees through reclaim.
Per node slab list state. It holds a list lock, a partial slab count and list, plus debug only totals for slab count and object count and a list of full slabs.

Flush coordination state. A workqueue pointer serves sheaf flushing, a per CPU work item carries owning cache and a skip marker, a mutex serializes flush operations and a per CPU instance anchors the work.

Deferred per CPU free batching and its reclaim flush helper. The structure aggregates three lockless lists for ordinary objects, objects freed by reclaim context and reclaim sheaves, plus an irq work item that drives processing. One configuration provides only the layout while another provides the per CPU instance wired to its handler.
Single object deferred free record. It pairs a reclaim head with the object pointer to be released after a grace period.
Slab state flag aliases. Locked, partial and pfmemalloc conditions reuse specific page flag positions for historical reasons.

Compile time selection stubs. Forced inlining, debug enablement, NUMA strictness, sysfs and debugfs initialization, probe attach and padding checks each provide two alternative definitions selected by configuration, with disabled cases reducing to empty operations or constant defaults.

Barn list extraction runs under interrupt saving spin protection. The helper first peeks at full and empty counts without locking and returns empty when both appear zero, otherwise it takes the barn lock, prefers removing the first full sheaf and otherwise the first empty sheaf, decrements the matching counter and releases the lock.

Partial list counting holds the node list lock across traversal. The helper takes the per node lock with interrupts saved, walks the partial list applying a caller supplied counter to each slab, accumulates the sum, releases the lock and returns the total.

Per CPU sheaf access uses a local lock with try semantics on allocation and full acquisition on flush. The main sheaf is guaranteed present while unlocked, spare and deferred reclaim pointers are detached under lock then processed outside the lock, including flushing unused objects, releasing empty sheaves and queueing deferred reclaim callbacks.

Global and auxiliary serialization. Node barn creation and departed CPU flushing hold a global slab mutex. A dedicated flush mutex serializes flush work. A spin lock guards a global object bitmap. Hotplug setup uses an unlocked node mask precheck followed by a locked recheck to handle concurrency.

Bulk fastpath acquisition cycles through local and shared sheaf sources. From an unlocked start it tries the local lock and reports partial progress if contended, allocates from main when nonempty, otherwise swaps in a usable spare, otherwise exchanges the empty main with the node barn with spinning allowed, recording barn hit or miss. Barn miss releases the lock and returns partial progress for slab page fallback, while each successful batch updates size and repeats until the request is satisfied.

Deferred reclaim sheaf retirement prepares then discards. Preparation walks resident pointers, invokes memory accounting and tagging free hooks, validates each object with slab free checks in reclaim context and compacts out rejected entries while remembering whether any source slab carried pfmemalloc. The reclaim callback then runs preparation, flushes surviving objects as unused, and releases the empty container.

Sheaf flushing drains per CPU state in stages. Main flushing loops over bounded batches until empty. Full per CPU flushing detaches spare and deferred reclaim sheaves under lock, flushes and frees the spare outside the lock, queues the detached deferred sheaf for reclaim, then drains main. Offline CPU flushing performs the same detach and drain without taking the local lock. Workqueue handlers dispatch these paths per cache and a dedicated handler flushes only the deferred reclaim sheaf.

Debug option parsing resolves global versus filtered enablement. Empty input enables full debugging. Otherwise each section yields flags plus an optional slab list, sections without lists update global flags while sections with lists only mark filtered mode and may request early stack storage. When only filtered sections appear the prior global value is retained and the raw string is saved for later per cache matching, then global state and its enable branch are updated.

Shrinker scan accounting is budget driven. Each CPU contribution reduces the remaining scan count and increases the freed total. Iteration stops once the budget reaches zero or below. A zero total maps to a stop signal while any positive total is reported as reclaimed.

Reclaim initialization establishes per CPU readiness and bounded delay. The fill delay is forced into a nonnegative range capped at one hundred seconds, each possible CPU gets initialized batch work items linked back to their CPU state, cleared bulk and channel lists, initialized monitor and page cache workers and a ready marker, and shrinker registration only proceeds after successful shrinker allocation.

Post allocation charging distinguishes large contiguous allocations from small slab objects. Large allocations succeed immediately when already accounted, otherwise they charge the compound page and move the byte count from global unreclaimable slab state to the charged vector. Small objects succeed immediately for caches that need no object charging or when already charged, otherwise they delegate to the generic post allocation hook for a single object.

Object count and pfmemalloc handling are consistent across helpers. Free count is defined as total objects minus in use count. Reclaim preparation and sheaf prefill propagate a pfmemalloc marker when any source slab or refill path required it, with prefill first trying without memalloc allowance and only then retrying with it while marking the sheaf. Single slab reclaim frees through the slab release path in reclaim context.

Resource exhaustion and fallback are explicit. Barn allocation failure during CPU setup aborts with out of memory without marking the node ready. Shrinker allocation failure logs and leaves reclaim unregistered. Bulk allocation treats lock contention, missing barn support and empty barn as partial success rather than error. Statistical counters record fallback, barn miss and exchange failure for diagnosis.

Capacity and bound facts. Minimum partial slabs five in one build and zero in another. Maximum partial ten and zero respectively. Per node barn holds at most ten full and ten empty sheaves. Bulk batch limit thirty two. Partial scan cap ten thousand. Maximum objects per page thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty seven. Object packing shift sixteen with mask derived as two to that power minus one. Per location tracked addresses sixteen.

Flag composition and default facts. Default debug combines consistency checks, red zone, poison and user storage. Exchange exclusion combines consistency checks, user storage and trace. Metadata set combines red zone, poison and user storage. Object cgroup clear mask combines DMA, reclaimable, account, nofail, thisnode and compound flags. Double exchange support is either a dedicated slab flag bit or an unused marker. Object poison is a dedicated flag bit. Global debug defaults to full set in one build and zero in others with higher order disable following the same pattern. Slab node masks, per CPU random state and object bitmap sizing follow page object limits.
